basic_info.title: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models

method.notes: Establishes that LM cross-entropy loss scales as a power law in model size N, dataset size D, and compute C over 7+ orders of magnitude, with weak dependence on architectural shape at fixed N. Foundation for all model-sizing arguments. Used in run2_capacity_diagnosis_and_scaling_review.md to frame the N-vs-D allocation question for the 2.6M-param decoder-light WM on 8.2M Porto fixes.

gap_analysis.whats_missing: Not a map-matching paper; methodology reference for capacity/data sizing only.
gap_analysis.novelty_reasoning: Cited for the power-law form of loss-vs-scale; coefficients are LM-specific and do not transfer directly (see pearce_agent_world_model_scaling.json).

relevance.bmw_relevance: Indirect: informs whether per-city retraining budgets should buy parameters or data.

uncertain: Superseded on compute-optimal allocation by Chinchilla (hoffmann_chinchilla_compute_optimal.json); Kaplan's original N-heavy allocation is known to be off.
